title: Accelerated Life Testing Analysis Tool — Overview and definition
t: Accelerated Life Testing Analysis Tool — Overview and definition
description: Plans accelerated stress tests and extrapolates to use-condition life.
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Plans accelerated stress tests and extrapolates to use-condition life. An accelerated life testing tool plans HALT/HASS and ALT matrices, fits life-stress models (Arrhenius, Eyring, inverse power), and extrapolates to field life with confidence bounds. Real implementations include ReliaSoft Weibull++/ALTA, JMP, and Python lifelines. It validates acceleration assumptions and sizes samples for demonstration targets.
capabilities: Test planning: stress levels, sample allocation
Life-stress modeling: Arrhenius, Eyring, IPL, Coffin-Manson
Acceleration-factor calculation with confidence bounds
Step-stress and progressive-stress analysis
Demonstration test sizing for reliability targets

body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Teaching ladder for Accelerated Life Testing Analysis Tool, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Test planning: stress levels, sample allocation). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Test planning: stress levels, sample allocation and Life-stress modeling: Arrhenius, Eyring, IPL, Coffin-Manson. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Weibull reliability analysis program) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
